candidate.answerReason: Subtracting the two given identities gives (x₁−x₂)[3(x₁+x₂)−h] = 0. Since x₁≠x₂, their sum is h/3.

methods.label: Subtract to eliminate b
methods.explanation:
Both given expressions equal \(b\), so subtracting them removes \(b\):
\[
3(x_1^2-x_2^2)-h(x_1-x_2)=0.
\]
The difference-of-squares identity reveals the common factor \(x_1-x_2\):
\[
(x_1-x_2)\bigl[3(x_1+x_2)-h\bigr]=0.
\]
Because \(x_1\ne x_2\), we may divide by \(x_1-x_2\). Thus \(3(x_1+x_2)=h\), giving
\[
\boxed{x_1+x_2=\frac h3},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses subtraction of equalities, difference-of-squares factoring, and division by a known nonzero quantity.
